🇲🇽🚆 MEXICO CITY PUTS WORLD CUP MONEY INTO THE METRO, NOT A PARTY

Brugada's government rebuilt four Line 2 stations — Tasqueña, General Anaya, Ermita and Portales — for 2.2 billion pesos, with 1.5 billion of the World Cup host-city funds going into permanent track, electrical and fire-safety work. Over 100,000 daily riders benefit; Chabacano reopened June 23. «This is not superficial or cosmetic work,» Brugada said.

🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO TELLS ITS AMBASSADORS: GO TELL THE WORLD WHAT THE 4T BUILT

Foreign Secretary Roberto Velasco convened the heads of every Mexican diplomatic mission and ordered them to broadcast the government's record on welfare, security and the economy abroad. With the foreign right-wing press running disinformation campaigns against Sheinbaum, the SRE is done letting others write Mexico's story.

🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO'S NEW AMBASSADOR LANDS IN WASHINGTON

Roberto Lazzeri arrived in Washington today to take over Mexico's embassy in the US, replacing Esteban Moctezuma after five years. Sheinbaum picked the former Nafin and Bancomext chief specifically for the T-MEC renegotiation — his six stated priorities lead with defending the Mexican community in the US and modernizing consulates, then trade. PAN and PRI voted against his ratification; Morena, PVEM, MC and PT confirmed him.

🇲🇽📈 <u>MEXICO’S ECONOMY POSTED ITS BIGGEST MONTHLY JUMP IN FIVE YEARS</u>

The economy grew 1.2% in April — the strongest single month since March 2021 — and 2.2% year-on-year, beating forecasts, INEGI reported (El Economista). Industry led with 2.1% monthly growth, manufacturing up 1.2%. The “tariff recession” Washington’s hawks predicted keeps not showing up.

🇲🇽💊 <u>MEXICO MAKES TRAMADOL PRESCRIPTION-ONLY, GUARDING AGAINST AN OPIOID CRISIS</u>

From July 14, the opioid painkiller tramadol can only be sold with a prescription — fillable three times max, logged and sealed at authorized pharmacies — under a reform to the General Health Law. Mexico is acting early on a drug the US FDA flagged as addictive even at prescribed doses, refusing to repeat the American opioid catastrophe.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>MEXICO’S PUBLIC POWER COMPANY WILL REACH 99.99% ELECTRICITY COVERAGE BY 2028</u>

State utility CFE is investing 21.4 billion pesos in 45,182 electrification works to connect the 739,785 people still living without power — prioritizing Indigenous communities in Sonora, Sinaloa, Michoacán and the Sierra Tarahumara. “Development shouldn’t depend on your postal code, distance, or geography,” said CFE director Emilia Calleja. Energy as a right, delivered by the state — not sold off.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM: WE DIDN’T COME FOR APPLAUSE ABROAD, WE CAME TO SERVE THE PEOPLE</u>

Asked about her standing, Sheinbaum credited honesty, results, and closeness to the people — not foreign recognition: “We didn’t arrive to be recognized abroad; we arrived to maintain the principles.” She fired back at an opposition that travels overseas to badmouth Mexico while the welfare programs, scholarships, and public works keep landing at home.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>MEXICO ADDED 300,000 PUBLIC UNIVERSITY SEATS IN SIX YEARS</u>

Public university enrollment climbed from 3.1 million to 3.4 million students between 2019 and 2025 — 300,000 more young people in classrooms, per the Chamber of Deputies’ public finance center. Education as a right, not a commodity — the reverse of the neoliberal decades that priced the poor out of college.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>IRAN BASED ITS WORLD CUP TEAM IN MEXICO BECAUSE WASHINGTON WOULDN’T HAVE THEM</u>

US travel rules force Iran’s squad out of Los Angeles within hours of every match — so Team Melli made its home in Tijuana instead. “If Iran hadn’t counted on Mexico’s support for lodging at the World Cup, we might not be playing in it,” said Iran’s ambassador, calling Mexico “a friend in difficult times.” While the empire slams the door, Mexico opens one.

AP/PBS: Merlin the duck steals the spotlight at President Sheinbaum's news briefing
June 22, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, the Guardian, PBS — all warm, all charmed. A viral World Cup duck in a green jersey waddles into the National Palace and the US press finds Mexico delightful. This is the coverage Mexico gets when the story isn't cartels. 🇲🇽
